new_defect_types.name: process_state_inconsistency
new_defect_types.description: An object shows the result of a process at a stage before that process happens (printed traces on the unwind/supply reel, sealant on parts not yet dispensed).
examples: phi221/gpt_image_2: supply reel already covered in circuit traces
phi221/flux3_klein: both reels and drum printed
phi221/gpt_image_2_quality_high: film leaving unwind reel already printed
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: A10 covers objects that could not work, A12 physics; neither covers cause-order of a depicted workflow. Proposed: extend A12 'cause produces effect' with 'effects must appear only downstream of their cause'.

new_defect_types.name: unrequested_slogan_and_branding_text
new_defect_types.description: Model fills walls, glass and machines with marketing slogans and real brand logos ('A CLEANER TOMORROW', 'HUMAN IN THE LOOP FOR A SAFER TOMORROW', KUKA, Henkel, TOYOTA, COGNEX).
examples: phi340/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'HUMAN IN THE LOOP FOR A SAFER TOMORROW', TOYOTA
phi101/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'SCA Bonding for a cleaner tomorrow', Henkel
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B07 lists template set dressing objects but not text; A03 only fires on pseudo-text, and these slogans are spelled correctly. A systematic stylistic tic of one model family goes unflagged.

new_defect_types.name: unrequested_thematic_text_overlay
new_defect_types.description: Equations / captions floating in the scene because they are stereotypically associated with the subject (Einstein -> E=mc²).
examples: orig469/qwen_image_2p1_pe: column of chalk equations and a graph
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: B04 only covers prompt words rendered as text; associated-concept text is not covered.

new_defect_types.name: material_weathering_leak
new_defect_types.description: Weathering specific to one material (bronze verdigris) spread onto an adjacent different material (granite base).
examples: orig583/flux3_klein: green patina blotches on gray stone base
new_defect_types.why_not_v2: Fits A22 in spirit but A22 examples are uniform grime/grain; add explicit 'material-specific wear on the wrong material' example.

rubric_issues.problem: Prompts asking for two people with matching outfits produce identical faces; v2 gives no severity or A06 vs A13 rule.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: State: identical face on 2+ people is A06 (moderate; major when they are the focal pair and also share pose), regardless of matching costume; A13 only for crowds of 3+.

rubric_issues.problem: Sign names in caps without quotes ('DO NOT ENTER sign') – unclear whether wording is required; half the models render a wordless roundel.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Treat unquoted sign names as type descriptors: missing wording is at most minor B04; quoted strings are required.

rubric_issues.problem: 'translucent hologram' is almost always rendered as an opaque planet; judges need an explicit check.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add translucency/holographic/glass looks to the B05 looks list: opaque rendering of a requested translucent element is a miss.

rubric_issues.problem: Dashcam timestamp OSD and similar genre UI is requested-genre content, not a watermark; but small generator sparkle logos in corners are real A16.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: A16 exception: overlays native to the requested capture genre (dashcam OSD, CCTV stamp, camera viewfinder) are not defects; explicitly list 'generator logo glyph in a corner' as A16.

rubric_issues.problem: Industrial prompts asking for 'wide shot showing rails, cable carriers' get close-ups; B08 examples focus on people.
rubric_issues.proposed_fix: Add example: requested wide/establishing shot rendered as a detail close-up, or a landmark whose full silhouette is requested cut by the frame, is major B08.

false_positive_traps.description: Dashcam hood/windshield edge occupying the bottom of frame and timestamp OSD are requested by 'dashcam image' – not A16/A17 occlusion.
Laika statue wearing a harness/vest is historically accurate, not an unrequested extra.
Paris storefront signs ('CAFE FLORE', 'LIBRAIRIE', 'PONT D'IENA') in Ghibli scenes are correct incidental text and scene-serving extras; don't flag as B07.
Inkjet/dispensing heads with visible thin fluid stream are plausible; only flag when the stream does not reach the work or falls from far above.
